title: urMQTT builder
lead: Configure your own urMQTT image: pick the options, add your certificates and keys, and download an ISO that is ready to boot. The work is done in this page.
privacy.title: Nothing leaves your browser.
privacy.text: Your certificates, private keys, settings and the finished ISO stay on your computer. The page only downloads the release files from this site, and it has no tracking and no third-party scripts.
unsupported: This browser lacks features the builder needs: {features}. Use a current version of Firefox, Chrome, Edge or Safari.
module-failed: The builder module could not be loaded: {reason}
release.title: Release
release.help: The template is the released urMQTT image with an empty configuration. It is downloaded from this site and checked against the release signature in your browser before anything is written into it.
release.failed: The list of releases could not be loaded ({reason}).
release.failed-help: Nothing is fetched from GitHub in its place. If you already have a template ISO and its SHA256SUMS, you can use files from your computer.
release.none: No release with a configurable template has been published yet.
release.none-help: The releases listed below were built before the runtime configuration existed, so they cannot be configured here. This page will offer the first release that comes with a template ISO. Until then you can use files from your computer.
release.no-template: Built before the runtime configuration existed: it cannot be configured here.
release.no-slot: The image has no configuration slot: it cannot be configured here.
release.no-signature: The release has no signed checksums.
release.format-unsupported: Uses a configuration format this page does not know. A newer builder is needed.
release.unverified: The mirror could not verify this release, so it is not offered.
release.removed: Removed from GitHub. Kept only for reference.
release.key-note: Releases are checked against the signing key {key} that is built into this page.
release.verifying: Checking the signature of the checksums…
release.verified: The signature of the checksums is valid (key {key}).
release.former-test-key: signed with the project's former test key
release.key-note-test: Releases {from} to {to} were signed with the project's former test key {key}, which the page accepts for those releases only.
release.verified-test-key: The signature of the checksums is valid (key {key}: signed with the project's former test key, accepted for {from} to {to} only).
release.local-unverified: This file has no signed checksums, so it cannot be checked against a release.
preset.title: Start from
preset.help: A preset only sets a few values. Everything else stays at its default, and you can change any field below.
preset.lab.desc: Address from DHCP, the diagnostic boot entry enabled. For a VM on a laptop or a lab server.
preset.vps.desc: Fixed address and gateway from your provider, a larger heap.
preset.auto.desc: Try DHCP first and fall back to a fixed address when there is no lease.
preset.confirm: Choosing a preset replaces the values you changed. Certificates and keys you imported are kept.
form.title: Configuration
section.reset-files: The section also holds certificates or keys you imported. Resetting removes them from this page.
field.range.network.mtu: 0 (the default): the MTU the network announces by DHCP, else 1500. Other values: 576 to 9000 bytes.
list.copy-default: Copy the defaults into the box
file.key-forgotten: Not kept after a reload: choose the private key again.
enum.network.mode.auto: DHCP first, then the fixed address
enum.storage.mode.disk: data partition on the boot disk
enum.storage.mode.auto: disk; RAM only for the ISO's live entry
enum.tls.identity_field.cn: common name of the client certificate
enum.tls.identity_field.san_uri: URI in the subject alternative name
enum.registry.mode.open: any device with a valid certificate
enum.console.virtio_gpu.auto: when the boot screen is dead
enum.websocket.auth.mtls: client certificate, as on the TLS port
enum.limits.publisher_backpressure.singl: pause a publisher whose only subscriber is full
enum.limits.publisher_backpressure.off: always read; drop for a slow subscriber
err.enum: Not one of the allowed values.
bar.title: Summary
bar.no-release: There is no release to build from yet.
bar.name: Name
reset.confirm: All settings, certificates, keys and the signing key are removed from this page.
progress.title: Build progress
result.title: Your ISO is ready
result.stale: The form changed after this ISO was built. Build again to apply the changes.
result.compare: The broker prints the configuration fingerprint at every boot. If it differs from this one, the machine is not running this configuration.
build.failed-help: Nothing was changed on your computer. You can try again, or use files from your computer instead.
risk.title: Please confirm
risk.intro: These choices are allowed but deserve a second look:
risk.cannot-serve.title: The image will not serve yet
risk.cannot-serve.text: Missing: {missing}. Without a server certificate, its private key and at least one operational CA the broker boots but refuses to serve. You can build again later with them.
risk.ram-storage.title: Data is kept in RAM only
risk.ram-storage.text: With storage mode "ram" retained messages and sessions are lost at every restart.
risk.wide-acl.title: Devices may reach every topic
risk.wide-acl.text: The rules in {keys} contain # at the top level. Any device with a valid certificate could then read or write all topics.
risk.watchdog-reset.title: A stuck handler resets the machine
risk.watchdog-reset.text: With the action "reset" the broker restarts when a handler runs over its time budget.
risk.cpu-disable.title: CPU features are switched off
risk.cpu-disable.text: Without the hardware accelerators TLS is slower. Use this only to work around a faulty accelerator.
risk.no-time.title: No time servers
risk.no-time.text: The clock is the machine's own. Certificate validity is checked against it, so a wrong clock can reject good certificates.
risk.no-control.title: No control key
risk.no-control.text: Without it devices cannot be revoked while the broker runs; revoking needs a new image.
risk.registry-open.title: Open device registry
risk.registry-open.text: Every device with a certificate from your CA may connect. Use the allowlist to admit listed identities only.
risk.entropy-none.title: No entropy fallback
risk.entropy-none.text: Without a hardware random source (virtio-rng, RDRAND) the broker refuses to boot.
risk.entropy-jitter.title: Random numbers may come from CPU jitter
risk.entropy-jitter.text: Without virtio-rng or RNDR/RDRAND on the host, the generator is seeded from CPU timing jitter and the firmware's values, which is weaker than a hardware source. Choose "Require a hardware random number generator" to refuse such hosts.
integrity.title: Integrity report
integrity.slots-text: {n} copies written, {m} bootloader hash references updated
integrity.sig-ok: The signature over SHA256SUMS is valid (key {key}).
integrity.not-checked: The release has not been checked yet.
integrity.template-ok: The downloaded template has the signed SHA-256.
integrity.template-bad: The downloaded template does NOT have the signed SHA-256.
integrity.overridden: You chose to continue after a failed check.
integrity.verified-image: The configured image was read back and its slots and bootloader hashes are consistent.
integrity.key-kind-test: the project's former test key (accepted for {from} to {to} only)
integrity.pubkeys-help: These are the keys built into the page, each with the releases it may sign. Compare them with minisign.pub and the keys/ directory in the repository and with SECURITY.md on GitHub.
integrity.offline: You can repeat the check on your own computer:
integrity.failed: The template could not be proven to be the signed release.
integrity.signature-failed: The signature of the checksums is not valid: {reason}
integrity.hash-mismatch: The download has SHA-256 {got}, the signed checksums say {want}.
integrity.override-help: Do not continue unless you know why. An ISO built from a template that does not match the release carries no guarantee about its kernel.
next.title: What to do next
next.intro: Your image is a normal bootable ISO.
next.step1.text: Keep it private: it contains your server's private key.
next.step2: Attach it as a CD or DVD and boot
next.step2.text: The image boots on x86-64 (BIOS or UEFI) and arm64 (UEFI). In a VM attach it as a CD drive; at a provider upload it as a custom ISO; on hardware write it to a USB stick.
next.step3: Compare the fingerprint on the console
next.step3.text: At boot the console prints a line starting with "config: fingerprint". It must be:
next.signed: The image is signed; the console also prints "signed by key {id}".
next.step4.text: From another machine, with a client certificate from your CA:
next.step5.text: Choose "Install urMQTT" in the boot menu to copy the image, with its configuration, to the machine's disk.
next.no-official-hash: A configured image has no official hash: it contains your configuration. What is signed is the template and, in your hands, the fingerprint above.
toml.title: Import or export TOML
toml.export-help: Only the values you changed are written. The command line tool reads this file.
toml.export-files: Only the values you changed are written. Put these files next to it: {names}.
toml.import-help: Choose or paste a config.toml. It replaces the values you changed; certificates and keys are read from the files you choose afterwards.
toml.needs-files: The file names these files: {names}. Choose them here to import them too.
toml.choose-files: Choose the files the TOML names
local.title: Use files from my computer
local.help: Choose a template ISO (urmqtt-template-…-universal.iso). Add SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.minisig of the same release to have it checked.
local.warn: Without the checksums and their signature the file cannot be checked.
local.both: Give both SHA256SUMS and its signature, or neither.
cert.help.cert: The certificate the broker presents to clients, as PEM. Put intermediate certificates after it in the same file.
cert.help.key: The private key of the server certificate, unencrypted PEM (ECDSA P-256). It is written into the image in the clear, as it was when it was compiled in.
cert.help.operational: The CAs that sign your device certificates. The broker accepts a client only if its certificate chains to one of them. Up to 8.
cert.help.bootstrap: CAs for provisioning only: their certificates may use provision/{id}/# and nothing else. Optional.
cert.help.control: The Ed25519 public key that verifies signed control messages (revocation, allowlist). A private key is accepted too; only its public half is kept.
cert.help.signing: An Ed25519 private key that signs the configuration. The broker verifies it at boot and prints the signer's key id. Optional.
cert.drop: Drop a file here or click to choose one
cert.drop-many: Drop files here or click to choose them
cert.too-big: The file is too large for a certificate.
cert.local-only: Parsed in this page. Nothing is uploaded.
cert.subject: Subject
cert.is-a-key: This is a private key, not a certificate.
cert.is-a-cert: This is a certificate, not a private key.
cert.too-short: Expires in {days} days. The build requires at least {need}.
cert.unsupported-key: The key is {type}. The broker's TLS uses ECDSA P-256 certificates only.
cert.is-ca: This is a CA certificate. The broker needs a server (leaf) certificate.
cert.no-names: The certificate names no host or address (subject alternative name). Clients that check the server name will refuse it.
cert.chain: The file holds a chain of {n} certificates.
cert.key-matches: The private key belongs to the server certificate.
cert.key-mismatch: The private key does not belong to the server certificate. Every TLS handshake would fail.
cert.signed-by-ca: The server certificate is signed by one of your operational CAs.
cert.not-signed-by-ca: The server certificate is not signed by your operational CAs. That is fine if your devices trust it another way.
cert.not-a-ca: This certificate is not marked as a CA.
cert.key-private: Private key: kept in this page only, never stored and never in the address.
control.from-private: A private key was given; only its public half is kept.
sign.private: Private key: kept in this page only, never stored and never in the address. The image carries the public key and the signature.
sign.generate-help: Creates a key pair in this browser and downloads the private key. Keep it: you need it to sign again.
emulator.title: Try in the emulator
emulator.hint: Starts the ISO you just built in an emulator inside this page.
emulator.unavailable: The emulator is not available here: {reason}
emulator.no-runtime: this build of the page does not include it.
emulator.no-isolation: the page is not cross-origin isolated, which the emulator's threads need (SharedArrayBuffer).
emulator.phone: it needs a desktop browser with at least 4 GB of memory.
emulator.note: This starts the image you just built in an x86-64 emulator that runs inside this page (WebAssembly). The console appears below. Nothing is sent anywhere.
emulator.limit-size: The emulator is loaded only now: about 3 MB the first time, then kept by your browser.
emulator.limit-slow: It is far slower than real hardware and keeps two processor cores busy while it runs. Time or speed seen here says nothing about the broker's performance.
emulator.limit-memory: It needs about 1.5 GB of memory. Closing this window stops it and frees the memory.
emulator.limit-network: It has no network: the broker starts and listens, but nothing can connect to it. Use it to see that the image boots and what its console says.
emulator.too-big: This image asks for a kernel heap of {heap} MB; the emulator can give its machine 1 GB of memory, so the image cannot boot here.
emulator.skip: Skip the 10 second countdown of the boot menu
emulator.licence: The emulator is QEMU compiled to WebAssembly (GPL-2.0).
emulator.serial: Serial console of the emulated machine
emulator.fp-ok: The kernel printed the same configuration fingerprint as this page.
emulator.fp-bad: The kernel printed fingerprint {got}…, this page has {want}…: it is not the configuration you built.
emulator.ready: The broker reports that it is ready.
emulator.refuses: The kernel refuses to serve (a server certificate, its key and a CA are missing, or the configuration is incomplete).
plaintext.on.title: Switch on plaintext MQTT?
plaintext.on.lead: Plaintext MQTT is not encrypted. Please read this first.
plaintext.on.point1: Nothing is encrypted. Anyone on the network path can read and change the messages.
plaintext.on.point2: A device is known only by its password or its address. Nothing else proves who it is.
plaintext.on.point3: Use it only on a network you control.
plaintext.on.point4: You must also list the networks that may connect (allow_from, for example 10.0.0.0/8). Without it the configuration is refused.
plaintext.anywhere.title: Accept connections from anywhere?
plaintext.anywhere.lead: This is dangerous. Every address could then connect without encryption.
plaintext.anywhere.point1: Never use this on a machine with a public address.
plaintext.anywhere.point2: Anyone on the Internet could try to connect, and read and change your messages.
plaintext.anywhere.point3: The kernel prints a loud warning at every boot.
plaintext.banner: Not encrypted. Anyone on the network path can read and change this traffic.
plaintext.banner-more: Use it only on a network you control.
plaintext.banner.anywhere: Danger: connections are accepted from every address, without encryption.
plaintext.banner.anywhere-more: Never do this on a machine with a public address.
plaintext.forgotten: The accounts are not kept across a reload: add them again.
plaintext.password-help: Press Enter or leave the field to set it. It is stored only as a hash.
plaintext.generated: Generated. Copy it now: after you set it, it cannot be shown again.
plaintext.pw-set: Password set, stored as a PBKDF2-SHA-256 hash. It cannot be shown again.
websocket.note: Password logins over WebSocket stay inside TLS, but a browser shows no certificate: list the web pages that may connect in origins (for example https://app.example.com). Without them the configuration is refused.
list.hint.cidr: One network per line, for example 10.0.0.0/8.
list.hint.ip_identity: One entry per line: a network, a space, then the identity, for example 10.0.1.0/24 plc.
preset.plaintext-note: No preset switches on plaintext MQTT. It stays off until you turn it on in its own section.
enum.plaintext.auth.password: a user name and password per client
enum.plaintext.auth.anonymous: no login; all clients share one identity
enum.plaintext.auth.ip: the client's address decides who it is
risk.plaintext-on.title: Plaintext MQTT is on
risk.plaintext-on.text: Messages on the plaintext port are not encrypted. Anyone on the network path can read and change them. Use it only on a network you control.
risk.plaintext-anywhere.title: Plaintext MQTT accepts every address
risk.plaintext-anywhere.text: With allow_from_anywhere any address may connect without encryption. Never use this on a machine with a public address. The kernel prints a warning at every boot.
risk.plaintext-anonymous.title: Plaintext clients need no login
risk.plaintext-anonymous.text: With auth "anonymous" every client that reaches the port gets the same identity. Only the allowed networks protect it.
risk.plaintext-public-address.title: The machine has a public address
risk.plaintext-public-address.text: The address {address} is not a private one. Plaintext MQTT on a public address can be reached from the Internet unless a firewall stops it.
simple.where.vps: A server with a fixed address
simple.where.vps.desc: A VPS or cloud server. You know its IP address and gateway.
simple.where.lab: A VM or a lab machine
simple.where.lab.desc: The address comes from DHCP. A diagnostic entry is added to the boot menu.
simple.where.auto: DHCP first, then a fixed address
simple.where.auto.desc: Asks DHCP and falls back to the fixed address you give if there is no answer.
simple.address.help: Your hosting provider gives you both.
simple.certs.help: Drop the server certificate, its private key and the CA certificate here, all together. They are sorted by what they contain and never leave this page.
simple.certs.drop: Drop your files here or click to choose them
simple.certs.missing.key: Still missing: the server's private key
simple.certs.missing.ca: Still missing: the CA certificate that signed your devices' certificates
simple.certs.nothing: No usable certificate or key was found in: {files}
simple.certs.key-forgotten: A private key is not kept when the page is reloaded: drop it again.
simple.certs.test: No certificates yet? See how to make test certificates
simple.title.name: Name your image
simple.extra.diagnostic: Diagnostics: add a boot menu entry that checks the hardware
simple.entropy.title: Random numbers
simple.entropy.jitter.desc: Boots on hosts without a hardware random number generator, seeding the generator from CPU timing jitter and the firmware's values; weaker than a hardware source.
simple.entropy.none: Require a hardware random number generator
simple.entropy.none.desc: The image refuses to boot without virtio-rng or a CPU instruction (RNDR, RDRAND/RDSEED) and says so on the console.
simple.entropy.warn: Warning: on a host with neither virtio-rng nor RNDR/RDRAND, this broker's random numbers (including those for TLS) are seeded from CPU timing jitter, a source weaker than hardware. Ask your provider for virtio-rng, or require a hardware generator so that such hosts are refused.
bar.next-address: Next: enter the server's address and gateway
adv.hint: Every option, search, TOML import and export.
adv.search.ph: Search, for example port, timeout, certificate
emulator.entry.diag-note: It draws the hardware report and runs the benchmarks; under emulation they finish in about 20 seconds. The numbers describe the emulator, not your hardware and not the broker.
emulator.entry.diag-off: This image was built without Diagnostics (see Extras), so this entry only stops and says why.
emulator.keys-hint: Click the screen to send your keyboard to the machine (letters, arrow keys, Enter, Escape). Tab leaves the screen.
simple.listener.tls.help: Encrypted. Every device proves itself with its own certificate. Needed for operators, services and remote control.
simple.listener.plain: Plain MQTT without TLS (port 1883, trusted networks only)
simple.listener.plain.help: Not encrypted: anyone on the network path can read and change the messages. Use it only on a network you control. It can be on at the same time as TLS.
simple.listener.one: At least one of the two must stay on.
simple.tls-off.note: With TLS off there are no operator, service or control rights at all (they need mutual TLS), no $SYS topics and no console. A device is known only by the way it logs in on the plain port.
simple.plain.title: Plain MQTT
simple.plain.networks.help: One network per line. It is filled in with the three private ranges: change it to the network your devices are on.
simple.plain.auth.password: User name and password (an account for each device or group)
simple.plain.auth.anonymous: No login: all devices share one identity
simple.plain.auth.ip: By network: the address decides who a device is
release.no-tls-off: Too old for an image with TLS off: that needs v0.2.1 or newer.
bar.needs-newer: Turning TLS off needs a release of v0.2.1 or newer.
bar.next-networks: Next: say which networks may connect
bar.next-account: Next: add an account for the devices
risk.tls-off.title: The TLS listener is off
risk.tls-off.text: Only plain MQTT is served: no mutual TLS, so no operator, service or control rights, no $SYS topics and no console, and nothing is encrypted. Devices are known only by their login on the plain port.
